draft.title: Qin Shi Huang
card: Qin Shi Huang was the ruler of the state of Qin. In 221 BCE he defeated the other warring states and united China. He became its first emperor.
He made one system for the whole empire. Writing, money and measures were standardised, so people in different places used the same ones.
His workers began linking older walls along the northern border into one long barrier. This became the start of the Great Wall.
When he died, he was buried in a huge tomb. Thousands of life-sized clay soldiers, the Terracotta Army, were placed nearby to guard him.
draft.remember: Qin Shi Huang united China in 221 BCE and used one system for writing, money and measures.

a.q: Why did Qin Shi Huang standardise writing, money and measures?
opts: To make the empire work as one country
To stop people from trading with other lands
To help the warring states rule themselves
To make the Great Wall quicker to build
a.why: Using the same writing, money and measures made it easier to govern and trade across the empire. The warring states had been defeated, so he was not giving them power to rule themselves.
a.clue: Think about ruling one large country, not many small ones.

b.q: Before 221 BCE, a trader in one Chinese state used coins that traders in another state did not accept. Which action by Qin Shi Huang would help solve this problem?
opts: Making one type of money for the whole empire
Linking walls along the northern border
Burying clay soldiers near his tomb
Defeating the other warring states in battle
b.why: One type of money meant coins were accepted everywhere in the empire, so trade was easier. Defeating the other states united China, but it did not by itself change the coins. The walls were for defence, not trade.
b.clue: Which action changed what people used to pay for goods?

wants.brief: A photo of the Terracotta Army near the tomb of Qin Shi Huang in Shaanxi, China, showing rows of life-sized clay soldiers in pits.
wants.why: It lets students see the scale and detail of the army buried to guard the emperor.

a.best: To make the empire work as one country

b.best: Making one type of money for the whole empire
